question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the **exact** values of $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=3{x}^{2}-2x-6$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $6$ are

$c=$
{{field-1}} $\,$ and  $\,c=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 6 & =\frac{1}{c-0}{\int }_{0}^{c}(3{x}^{2}-2x-6)\,\text{d}x \\ 6 & ={\frac{1}{c}({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-6x)|}_{0}^{c} \\ 6 & =\frac{1}{c}[({c}^{3}-{c}^{2}-6c)-0] \\ 6c & ={c}^{3}-{c}^{2}-6c \\ 0 & ={c}^{3}-{c}^{2}-12c \\ 0 & ={c}^{2}-c-12 \\ 0 & =(c-4)(c+3) \\ c & =-3,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in **ascending order**, the values of $c$ are 

$$
c=-3\,\text{and}\,c=4.
$$
